request.what: Reduce the committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes only the committeeMinSize parameter from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize of 7.
A single resignation or term expiration under the current setting could make governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval ineligible for ratification.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer allowing governance to continue if one or two current committee members retire or expire.
The proposal depends temporally on enactment of another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model updates, with no claimed technical interaction between the parameter changes.
The change does not directly alter the current number of Constitutional Committee members or the maximum possible number of members.
At a committee size of 5 and a 2/3 voting threshold, 4 Constitutional votes meet the threshold and 2 Unconstitutional votes can prevent it.
The proposal says the current elections process is intended to maintain a 7-seat Constitutional Committee rather than lower the existing number of seats.
The proposer states the change has undergone Parameter Committee technical review through PCP-005 and links to a Cardano Forum discussion.

The proposer states the change is reversible if there are at least 7 Constitutional Committee members, but reverting to 7 when fewer than 7 members exist would immediately halt governance until enough members were elected.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change lowering committeeMinSize from 7 to 5 to reduce governance inoperability risk, while acknowledging changed voting dynamics and a conditional reversion risk.
